Pakistan clinch ODI Tri-Series title with three-wicket win over Sri Lanka in Lahore

02 Nov 2026, 08:23 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Editorial Desk · Source: www.bhaskar.com

2 min read

Key takeaways

Match Summary

  • Competition: ODI Tri-Series Final
  • Teams: Sri Lanka vs Pakistan
  • Venue: Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore
  • Format: 50 overs per side
  • Result: Pakistan won by 3 wickets (with 9 balls remaining)
  • Match Status: Completed

Sri Lanka Innings

  • Total: 325/8 in 50 overs
  • Toss: Sri Lanka batted first after losing the toss
  • Opening Partnership: Avishka Fernando (38 off 49) and Kamindu Mendis added 87 for the first wicket
  • Key Partnership: Kamindu Mendis (131 off 128, 12 fours, 2 sixes) and Pawan Rathnayake (77 off 65) put on 146 for the third wicket
  • Collapse: Sri Lanka lost 7 wickets for 70 runs in the final 10 overs
Explore this topicCricketPakistan Clinch ODI Tri-Series Title with Thrilling Run Chase Against Sri LankaPakistan Face Sri Lanka in Lahore Tri-Series ODI Final

Pakistan Innings

  • Target: 326 runs
  • Total: 331/7 in 48.3 overs
  • Early Setback: Both openers dismissed for 14 runs (Maaz Sadaqat and Babar Azam – Azam out for a duck)
  • Recovery Stand: Fakhar Zaman (127 off 99, 11 fours, 6 sixes) and Saud Shakeel (74 off 75) added 149 for the third wicket
  • Finish: Arafat Minhas (61* off 31, 3 fours, 4 sixes) and Hasan Nawaz (37* off 65) shared an unbroken 94-run stand for the sixth wicket to seal the chase

Bowling Figures (Pakistan)

  • Shaheen Afridi: 2 wickets
  • Naseem Shah: 2 wickets
  • Salman Agha: 2 wickets
  • Haris Rauf: 2 wickets

Key Performances

  • Player of the Match (likely): Fakhar Zaman for his match-winning century under pressure
  • Top Scorer (Sri Lanka): Kamindu Mendis – 131
  • Top Scorer (Pakistan): Fakhar Zaman – 127
  • Best Bowling (Pakistan): Four bowlers shared two wickets each; no single standout figure

Practical Implications

  • Pakistan secure the tri-series trophy ahead of upcoming ODI assignments.
  • Fakhar Zaman’s form and the middle-order resilience (Minhas, Nawaz) are positive signs for Pakistan’s batting depth.
  • Sri Lanka’s top-order promise (Mendis, Rathnayake) contrasts with a fragile lower order that collapsed at the death.
  • Teams and analysts should review the death-bowling strategies of both sides given the high-scoring finish.
